newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain six month T-bill yields to see record lows.
newsitem.headline: Spain six month T-bill yields to see record lows.

text.p: Six-month Spanish Treasury bill yields could set a new low at Wednesday's auction, falling from the previous sale's level of 6.581 percent, dealers predicted on Tuesday.
On the grey market the yield on the bills slipped to below 6.30 percent by 1220 GMT, after trading around 6.35/40 percent early on Tuesday.
"There has been good demand by investment funds and that pushed down the yields on the grey market," a dealer said.
"The rates on deposits declined sharply, especially after October CPI sparked expectations of a fresh rate cut before year end" another dealer added.

Lower-than-expected Spanish CPI data released last week raised hopes that the Bank of Spain could sanction its seventh rate cut this year -- of at least 25 basis points -- analysts said. CPI posted a 0.1 percent month-on-month rise for October and 3.5 percent year-on-year rise.
At the previous auction on November 6, six-month bills were unchanged at their previous record low of 6.581 percent.
Last week the one-year bill auction set a new record low at 6.48 percent. In Tuesday morning trade one-year bills, which will also be tendered next week, were trading at 6.15/20 percent.
